- **Album of the Year:** Henry Mancini, for *The Music from Peter Gunn* ('Album of the Year' went to Henry Mancini's The Music from Peter Gunn.)
- **Best Album Cover:** Frank Sinatra, for *Only the Lonely* (He won his first GRAMMY not for singing, but rather as art director for his Only the Lonely album).
- **Best Male Pop Vocal:** Perry Como, "Catch A Falling Star" (Perry Como won the 1959 Grammy Award for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance).
- **Best Female Pop Vocal:** Ella Fitzgerald, for *Ella Fitzgerald Sings The Irving Berlin Song Book* (Ella Fitzgerald won the 1959 Grammy Award for Female Pop Vocal Performance).
- **Best Country & Western:** The Kingston Trio, "Tom Dooley" (The Kingston Trio won the 1959 Grammy Award for Best Country & Western Performance with "Tom Dooley").
- **Best R&B:** The Champs, "Tequila" (The Champs won the 1959 Grammy Award for Best R&B Recording).
- **Best Recording for Children:** David Seville and the Chipmunks, "The Chipmunk Song" (David Seville And The Chipmunks (Ross Bagdasarian, Sr.) won the 1959 Grammy Award).
- **Best Pop Duo/Group Vocal:** Keely Smith and Louis Prima, "That Old Black Magic" (Keely Smith, Louis Prima won the 1959 Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance By A Duo Or Group With Vocal).

- **Spoken Word:** Stan Freberg, for *The Best of the Stan Freberg Shows* (Stan Freberg for The Best of the Stan Freberg Shows).

Guitar Slim (Eddie Jones) wrote "The Things That I Used to Do" and released it on Specialty Records in 1953, with Ray Charles on piano and as arranger and producer. The song became a 1954 bestseller. Sources disagree on the recording date: one gives October 16, 1953 and another October 26, 1953.

- **Release and sales:** The [Wikipedia article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Things_That_I_Used_to_Do) gives 1953 as the release year and notes that the single became a bestseller the following year. [Cavac](https://cavac.at/cavacopedia/Guitar%20Slim) credits the song with spending weeks at number one on the Billboard R&B chart and selling over a million copies. [Find a Grave](https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/14769510) says it was the year's best-selling R&B single and spent 14 weeks at number one.
- **Recording:** [Blues.org](https://blues.org/?p=14018) says Ray Charles played piano on the record. The [Wikipedia article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Things_That_I_Used_to_Do) says he arranged and produced the session at J&M Studio in New Orleans. Dates given are October 16 ([Wikipedia mirror](https://www.chise.org/ipfs/QmXoypizjW3WknFiJnKLwHCnL72vedxjQkDDP1mXWo6uco/wiki/The_Things_That_I_Used_to_Do.html)), October 26 ([Daily Kos](https://www.dailykos.com/stories/2023/12/10/2207009/-Black-Music-Sunday-Remembering-Guitar-Slim-and-the-things-he-used-to-do)), and October 27 ([Ray Charles discography site](https://raycharles.cydstumpel.nl/?p=2102)).
- **Honors:** The song was inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame in 1984 under the Classics of Blues Recording category ([Blues.org](https://blues.org/?p=14018)).
- **Artist background:** [Cavac](https://cavac.at/cavacopedia/Guitar%20Slim) gives Eddie Jones's dates as December 10, 1926 to February 7, 1959, and says he was born in Greenwood, Mississippi. Several artists, including Buddy Guy and Albert Collins, have cited him as an influence ([NTS](https://www-integration.nts.live/artists/56424-eddie-guitar-slim-jones)).
